q: In the days of the judges, why did Naomi's family leave Bethlehem?
why: There was not enough food in the land.
quote: there was a famine in the land.

q: During the famine, where did Naomi's family go to live?
why: There her sons married Moabite women.
quote: went to reside in the land of Moab.

q: When Naomi told her to go home, what did Ruth promise her?
a: Wherever you go, I will go
wrong: I will go back to Moab
why: Ruth would not leave her mother-in-law.
quote: For wherever you go, I will go

q: Ruth told Naomi, “Your people will be my people, and your God will be…” what?
why: Ruth chose to follow the God of Israel.
quote: your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.

q: When Naomi urged her daughters-in-law to go home, what did Orpah do?
why: But Ruth clung to Naomi.
quote: and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.

q: In Bethlehem, what did Ruth go into the fields to do?
why: Poor people gathered leftover grain after the harvesters.
quote: Please let me go into the fields and glean heads of grain

q: In Bethlehem, whose field did Ruth happen to glean in?
why: Boaz was from the clan of Naomi's husband.
quote: And she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz

q: Why was Boaz so kind to Ruth in his field?
a: She had been kind to Naomi
why: He had heard how she left her own land for Naomi.
quote: I have been made fully aware of all you have done for your mother-in-law

q: At the end of the book of Ruth, whom did Ruth marry?
why: The LORD gave them a son.
quote: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife.

q: Ruth's son Obed became the grandfather of which famous king?
why: A Moabite woman became part of King David's family.
quote: He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.

q: In the book of Ruth, what was the name of Naomi's husband?
why: He died in Moab.
quote: The man’s name was Elimelech, his wife’s name was Naomi

q: What were the names of Naomi's two Moabite daughters-in-law?
why: Both were women of Moab.
quote: one named Orpah and the other named Ruth.

q: When Naomi came back to Bethlehem, what did she ask the women to call her instead?
why: She felt the Almighty had dealt bitterly with her.
quote: Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.

q: Naomi said she went away full, but the LORD brought her back how?
why: She had lost her husband and both sons.
quote: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty.

q: At what time of year did Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem?
why: It was the right time for Ruth to glean.
quote: And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

q: How was Boaz related to Naomi?
a: A relative on her husband's side
why: He was from the clan of Elimelech.
quote: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side

q: In his field, what did Boaz tell Ruth to do when she was thirsty?
a: Drink from the young men's jars
why: Boaz made sure she was cared for.
quote: And when you are thirsty, go and drink from the jars the young men have filled.

q: When Boaz showed her kindness, what did Ruth say she was?
why: She was amazed he noticed her.
quote: even though I am a foreigner?

q: Boaz told Ruth she had taken refuge under whose wings?
a: The LORD's, the God of Israel
why: Ruth had come to trust Israel's God.
quote: under whose wings you have taken refuge.

q: What did Naomi tell Ruth that Boaz was to their family?
why: A kinsman-redeemer could buy back family land.
quote: He is one of our kinsman-redeemers.

q: Where was Boaz winnowing barley the night Ruth went to see him?
why: Naomi told Ruth where to find him.
quote: tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.

q: On the threshing floor, what did Ruth ask Boaz to spread over her?
why: She was asking him to redeem her as a kinsman.
quote: Spread the corner of your garment over me, for you are a kinsman-redeemer.

q: Where did Boaz sit down to settle the matter of redeeming Naomi's land?
why: Legal matters were settled at the gate.
quote: Meanwhile, Boaz went to the gate and sat down there.

q: In old Israel, how did a man make a land deal legally binding?
a: Removed his sandal and gave it
why: This was a confirmation in Israel.
quote: a man would remove his sandal and give it to the other party

q: What was the name of the son born to Ruth and Boaz?
why: He became King David's grandfather.
quote: and they named him Obed.

q: What were the names of Naomi's two sons?
why: Both sons died in Moab.
quote: and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion.

q: About how long had Naomi's family lived in Moab when her sons died?
why: Naomi was left without husband or sons.
quote: And after they had lived in Moab about ten years

q: How much barley did Ruth gather on her first day in Boaz's field?
why: She worked in the field until evening.
quote: it was about an ephah of barley.

q: Why did the closer kinsman-redeemer refuse to redeem Naomi's land?
a: It would jeopardize his own inheritance
why: So Boaz became the redeemer.
quote: or I would jeopardize my own inheritance.

q: At the city gate, Boaz said Ruth was the widow of which man?
why: Boaz kept the dead man's name alive in Israel.
quote: I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife

q: Naomi's family were Ephrathites from which town?
why: They returned there after the famine.
quote: They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah

q: Who gave Ruth's baby the name Obed?
why: They said a son had been born to Naomi.
quote: The neighbor women said, “A son has been born to Naomi,” and they named him Obed.
